statement: Abyssinia was a Christian kingdom across the Red Sea whose king was titled the Negus (an-Najashi).
He told the Companions to go to Abyssinia, describing it as a land of truth whose king wronged no one.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq; narrated in indirect speech.

statement: The first group left in the fifth year of prophethood and included Uthman and Ruqayyah.
alternatives: Usually given as Rajab of the fifth year; twelve men and four women.

statement: A second group of more than eighty men, with women, followed, including Ja'far ibn Abi Talib.
alternatives: Counts vary: 82 or 83 men and 18 or 19 women.

statement: Umm Salamah narrated: Quraysh sent two envoys with gifts for the Negus and his generals asking for the emigrants to be handed over unheard; he refused until he had questioned them.
notes: Musnad Ahmad, hadith of Umm Salamah; isnad graded hasan by Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut (from memory). Not in the datasets, so not machine-checked. Held at grade C until the reviewer confirms number and grading. The envoys are named as Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah.

statement: Ja'far's address to the Negus: their former ignorance; the messenger known for lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness; what he called them to; their persecution; their choosing the Negus's land.
notes: Given in indirect speech and abridged, from memory. Reviewer to compare each item with the Arabic text.

statement: Ja'far recited from the opening of Surah Maryam; the Negus and his bishops wept; he said this and what Musa brought come from one lamp, and refused to hand them over.
notes: Reviewer to confirm which reading the reference text has.

statement: The envoys raised the matter of Isa; Ja'far said he is the servant of Allah, His messenger, His spirit and His word cast to the virgin Maryam; the Negus said Isa did not exceed that by a stick's length; the gifts were returned; the emigrants lived in safety.
Hamzah accepted Islam in this period.
alternatives: Usually dated to the end of the sixth year of prophethood.

statement: He prayed that Allah strengthen Islam with the more beloved of Abu Jahl or Umar; the more beloved was Umar.
notes: Machine-checked. Graded sahih by al-Albani and Ahmad Shakir. Tirmidhi 3683, which says Umar came the next day, is graded very weak and is not used.

statement: The detailed accounts of how Umar accepted Islam have weak chains.
notes: Editorial statement covering the story of his sister and Surah Ta-Ha and other accounts; reviewer to confirm the wording is fair.

statement: Ibn Umar, as a boy on the roof, saw the crowd saying Umar had left his religion, and al-As ibn Wa'il declare his protection, and the people disperse.
notes: Machine-checked. The quoted words of the crowd and of al-As follow the Arabic ('saba'a Umar'); reviewer to confirm the rendering.

statement: Ibn Mas'ud: we have been strong since Umar accepted Islam.
Some emigrants returned to Makkah; others, including Ja'far, stayed until after the Hijrah and came to Madinah at the time of Khaybar.
notes: Bukhari 3876 (Abu Musa) confirms Ja'far's stay until Khaybar; machine-checked.

statement: He announced the Negus's death on the day he died, said 'today a righteous man has died, rise and pray for your brother', and led the funeral prayer.
notes: Machine-checked. The narration names him Ashamah.
